title: The Parcel I Was Definitely Home For
scene: You stay home all morning for a parcel with a three-hour delivery window. After avoiding anything that might make you miss the intercom, you step into the kitchen for less than a minute and discover that the delivery attempt happened at exactly that moment.
sceneJa: 9時から12時の宅配を受け取るため午前中ずっと家にいる。インターホンを聞き逃さないよう細心の注意を払っていたのに、ほんの一瞬キッチンへ行った間に配達が来てしまう。

chunks.ja: 荷物が届く予定でした
そこで午前中の予定を組みました
家にいることを前提に

chunks.en: and turned the intercom volume up
chunks.ja: インターホンの音量を上げました

chunks.en: I even avoided taking a shower
chunks.ja: シャワーを浴びることさえ避けました
ヘッドホンをつけることも
呼び鈴が鳴った場合に備えて
追跡ページには表示されました

chunks.en: the parcel was out for delivery,
so I became unusually attentive to every sound outside.
chunks.ja: そこで外の物音すべてに妙に敏感になりました
キッチンへ行きました
スマホに通知が出ていました
起きたことを考え直してくれるかのように
ある意味では安心しました
結局は左右されるのだと分かって

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: I turned the intercom volume up / so as not to miss / the delivery driver
I turned / the intercom volume up so / as not to / miss the delivery driver
I turned the intercom / volume up so as / not to miss the / delivery driver
questions.explanation: ‘Turn the intercom volume up’ is one action, and ‘so as not to miss ...’ clearly expresses its purpose.

questions.question: What does ‘just in case the bell rang’ mean?
options: Because the bell had already rung
As a precaution in case the bell might ring
Because the speaker wanted the bell to ring
questions.explanation: ‘Just in case’ introduces a precaution taken because something might happen.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence dryly funny?
options: It treats an absurdly precise missed moment as reassuring information
It says delivery windows are always exactly thirty seconds long
It suggests the speaker was happy to miss the parcel
questions.explanation: The humour comes from calmly praising the precision of a system that required the speaker to be available for one tiny moment inside a three-hour window.

speak: Start practical and prepared. Let ‘just in case’ sound slightly cautious rather than dramatic. Pause after ‘The moment I came back’ so the missed delivery lands clearly. Read ‘as if either of them might reconsider what had happened’ with quiet disbelief. Deliver the final sentence in an almost approving tone; the understatement makes the irony work.
review: Flow: delivery window → careful preparation → increasing vigilance → thirty-second absence → missed delivery → calm bureaucratic irony. Useful chunks: ‘so as not to ...’, ‘just in case ...’, and ‘the moment ...’. Notice that the ending does not complain directly; it describes the absurd timing as if it were reassuring evidence of precision.
